title: RWA Weekly Holders Report With Token Terminal
description: Weekly holder growth across stablecoins, funds, U.S. T-bills, credit and stocks.

blocks.text: This is the weekly holders edition of RWA Activity on the Terminal, a joint report from RWA Foundation and Token Terminal. It tracks asset holder growth over the past 7 days across five categories: stablecoins, tokenized funds, tokenized U.S. T-bills, tokenized credit funds and tokenized stocks. Each category is broken down by issuer and by chain.

parts.text: This is the weekly holders edition of RWA Activity on the Terminal, a joint report from RWA Foundation and Token Terminal. It tracks asset holder growth over the past 7 days across five categories: stablecoins, tokenized funds, tokenized U.S. T-bills, tokenized credit funds and tokenized stocks. Each category is broken down by issuer and by chain.

blocks.text: All figures are taken strictly from Token Terminal as of October 5, 2026. Growth figures cover the 7-day window from September 28 to October 5. No third-party data has been added, and no figures have been adjusted or estimated.

blocks.text: Holders refers to addresses holding a non-zero balance, summed across assets without removing duplicates. Each chart shows the issuers or chains listed by Token Terminal for that category. Tokenized U.S. T-bills and tokenized credit funds are subsets of tokenized funds, so some issuers and chains appear in more than one category with the same figure.

blocks.text: Overview

parts.text: Overview

blocks.text: Stablecoins added far more holder addresses than any other category. Tether added about 1.6 million and Circle 636,000, and BNB Chain added about 1.6 million by chain. Tokenized stocks were next, with xStocks adding 144,700 holder addresses and Solana 228,100.

blocks.text: Tokenized funds moved in the hundreds. USDai added 576 holder addresses, the most of any fund issuer, and Arbitrum One added 629 by chain. Tokenized T-bill holder growth was concentrated in Ondo Finance (+167) and Sei EVM (+158).

blocks.text: Stablecoins

parts.text: Stablecoins

blocks.text: Tether added about 1.6 million stablecoin holder addresses over 7 days and Circle 636,000. The next issuer, Paxos, added 26,400. Phantom (+18,700) and World Liberty (+10,200) followed, then Sky (+8,800), United Stables (+2,700), Polymarket (+2,700), Ripio (+2,000) and Ethena (+1,000).

blocks.text: By chain, BNB Chain added about 1.6 million holder addresses, roughly eight times the next chain. Solana (+198,500) and Celo (+195,900) were close for second, followed by Tron (+151,000), Base (+130,500) and Arbitrum One (+93,300). Arc (+27,400), Robinhood Chain (+22,700), Algorand (+15,800) and Plasma (+8,700) completed the top 10.

blocks.text: Conclusion

parts.text: Conclusion

blocks.text: Stablecoins accounted for most of the week's new holder addresses, led by Tether and Circle by issuer and by BNB Chain by chain. Tokenized stocks followed, led by xStocks and Solana.

blocks.text: Tokenized fund holder growth was smaller in absolute terms and concentrated in a few names. USDai led by issuer and Arbitrum One by chain, in both tokenized funds overall and tokenized credit. In T-bills, Ondo Finance and Sei EVM accounted for nearly all of the growth.
